newsitem.title: USA: GM buys back $1.6 billion in stock in Q1.
newsitem.headline: GM buys back $1.6 billion in stock in Q1.

text.p: General Motors Corp said Monday it used about $1.6 billion to buy back more than 27 million shares of its $1-2/3 par value common stock during the first quarter.
The purchases occurred under the $2.5 billion stock buyback program approved by GM's board in January. The $1-2/3 par value shares represent GM's automotive shares.
GM had 747 million average shares outstanding in the 1997 first quarter, versus 755 million a year ago.
GM said it finished the first quarter with total cash and marketable securities of $14.6 billion.
That is up from $7.6 billion a year ago, but down from $17 billion as of December 31, 1996.
GM reported first quarter earnings from continuing operations of $1.80 billion, up from $800 million a year ago, which was held back by a 17-day strike.
